title: AI-assisted virtual screening identifies a dual-stage antimalarial candidate
summary: An AI-assisted virtual-screening cascade using shape-based and machine-learning models prioritized potential Plasmodium kinase inhibitors. Eight virtual hits were experimentally evaluated; LabMol-167 inhibited P. berghei ookinete conversion and P. falciparum blood-stage parasites at nanomolar concentrations and showed low cytotoxicity in mammalian cells. A possible additional PK5 target was proposed from computational target fishing and docking, not demonstrated experimentally. This is a preclinical hit result and does not establish therapeutic efficacy. The article appeared online on 2021-03-16.
ai_technology: AI-assisted virtual screening combining shape-based and machine-learning models

evidence.tested: Eight virtual hits were evaluated; LabMol-167 showed nanomolar activity in P. berghei ookinete conversion and P. falciparum blood-stage assays, with low mammalian-cell cytotoxicity.
evidence.unknown: The PK5 dual-target mechanism is proposed from computational target fishing and docking; in-vivo efficacy and clinical benefit are not established.
